content.thinking:
I'm starting to write the module, setting up vector helpers and importing the builder, frame, and math utilities needed for construction.

Still defining color ramps...

Still writing bark texture logic...

Setting up the build function with texel density calculations for paint resolution, then defining the hip joint and spine points along the koala's body for the skeleton structure.

I'm working out whether to split the spine and neck into separate bone chains or combine them into one smooth catmull-rom curve, deciding a single chain covering spine through neck segments is simpler for sweeping the body geometry.

Including hips is fine since it sits at the same spot as the first spine joint. I'm adding a stand joint parented to hips, and setting up a radius function with keyed interpolation points along the body to control the sweep's thickness at different points, then starting on head placement coordinates.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for building head geometry boxes, then working through ear shapes using a stepped profile with overlapping row widths to form the outline.

Positioning each ear with a rotation angle and extruding the shape along perpendicular directions to give it thickness, attaching it to the ear bone with fur color, then planning a textured inner ear plane sized to match the ear's diameter.

Writing pixel texture function...

Still writing the ear rim gradient logic... now planning the eyes, jaw, and stepped cheek tufts for each side of the face.

Setting three z-offset tufts with cream color, skipping the chin fluff and brow details. I'm planning the ear hinge joints (earL/earR with side sign), then moving to arms and grips—establishing the stand bone joint early so branch sweeps for the stand parts can reference it in their catmull-rom paths.

Working out tapering branch radii and trunk points...

Now I'm sizing the seat support post to span from y 0.1 to 0.45, overlapping the seat underside, and planning rope band boxes around the post using wood coloring.

I'll add four rope bands at spaced heights with a small hanging tassel near the post front, confirm the trunk-seat joint is seamless, and then move on to scattering fallen leaf cards across the base for extra detail.

For the leaf cards, I'm positioning them on the second tier with varied lean and flow directions so they look naturally scattered, then sizing them appropriately. I'll also scatter small gumnut spheres on the base and twigs, and write a twig/leaf generator function that recursively builds branch structures from a root point and direction.

Writing twig generator function...

Still working out leaf placement...

I'm gathering leaf frames into arrays, then adding tuft bodies, bark strips, and a scatter filter checking hit positions on the trunk. Now I'm drafting a reusable grip function that builds finger and thumb joints from parent joints, offsets, and sweep angles.

Writing digit placement logic...

Still working out joint names and palm geometry...

With W computed, I build the arm path through limb() for shoulder/elbow/hand, then pass that polyline into the chain function since point arrays work fine as paths. Then I sweep the arm with tapering radii from shoulder to wrist, using smooth interpolation and fur-colored segments, and I'm considering a rounded wrist cap.

For the legs, I'm setting up a three-point chain from hip to knee to ankle with similarly tapering radii, placing the hip joint inward on the body. I work out the foot placement using perpendicular direction vectors and derive a seat radius function that interpolates based on z-position along the body, settling on a linear taper formula for the body radius at the seat.

Now I'm positioning toe offsets along the foot, computing pad placement so toes don't clip into the body, and checking that thigh spacing relative to foot width looks anatomically right, reusing the same finger-offset math for toes before working out the ankle joint position relative to the knee.

Claws will be spikes anchored at the path endpoint, oriented along the tangent direction and rigged to the final joint bone. I'll skip whiskers and tail nub details for now.

I'm finalizing the color palette — dark nose and eye patches, gum tones, claw and twig colors, striped fur shades, and white highlights for textured areas.

Counting around a dozen textures needed for leaves, eyes, nose, mouth, ears, plaques, and tuft patterns, then checking that textured plane parts use the proper bone, direction, axis, and group parameters correctly before building the lathe-based base shape with its tiered outline.

I'm adding a moss paint rule for the base top face using noise thresholds, then moving on to sketch the `keyed` helper and the overall `b.cards` function signature covering frames, textures, and options like size, lean, flow, bend, and sink for tufts.

For the stand geometry, I'm using a bone-based sweep for the trunk path, then working out bark strip placement with box geometry — checking embed depth versus strip thickness so they don't float awkwardly on the curved trunk surface, accounting for sag across the strip width against the trunk radius.

Now I'm adding gum nuts as small flattened spheres at twig tip positions, planning ear geometry with an inner textured plane, and setting up the extrude options (bone, color, thickness) for ear shapes, plus cheek tufts attached to the head bone.

I'm working out crown tufts on top of the head using stepped extrudes arranged in rows with decreasing width, positioned at a few x-offsets to simulate a tufted fur pattern, while deciding to skip lower-lip fluff for now.

Now I'm sketching the remaining head layering: assigning fur, cheek, and muzzle materials to the cranium, crown, cheeks and muzzle, giving the jaw a cheek-colored paint, and placing eye patches and pupils as small colored planes positioned against the front face, checking the cranium's front z-coordinate lines up correctly.

I'm calculating positions for the muzzle, nose, and mouth so they attach properly to the cranium and cheeks without clipping, working out size and offset values for each facial feature's bounding box and corresponding texture plane.

Then I'm working out jaw placement, checking for overlap with the muzzle bottom and adjusting the jaw's center height to maintain a small gap between the two.

Good, the gap reads as a visible mouth slit from the front, recessed between jaw and muzzle, which works well with the mouth decal. The chin and jaw hinge placement look fine too, so now I'm moving to writing the final code, defining the spine radius keyframes along the body.

Still writing sweep logic...

I'm checking types along the way -- the radius function returns a proper tuple, the sweep runs across the hip-spine-neck bone chain, and the body surface is used for placing fur tufts, with digit helpers typed against Vector3 and the joint parent typing verified.

Writing arm placement code...

Scaling finger digits down to a chunky pixel look, then scattering bark strip details across the trunk surface with height and normal filters, and placing leaf twig clusters along the trunk path at a few key points.

Now I'm planning the fallen leaves lying flat on the ground, plus gum nuts and stepped pebble rocks scattered on the base, centering the koala and trunk at x=0, and getting ready to write out the complete file with strict TypeScript typing in mind.
